own_solution.law: Newton's second law along the incline with kinetic friction: a = g(sin theta - mu_k cos theta); constant-acceleration kinematics from rest: v^2 = 2 a d
assumptions: Coulomb kinetic friction with constant mu_k = 0.15
Block treated as a particle sliding (no rolling/tipping); no air resistance

T5DF8.regime: mu_s matters only if mu_s >= tan(30 deg) = 0.577 (block would not start sliding from rest); 0.35 < 0.577, so the block slides and the answer is unchanged

T263F.regime: mu_s matters only if mu_s >= tan(30 deg) = 0.577; 0.35 is below this, so the block starts sliding

notes: a = 9.8*(0.5 - 0.15*0.8660254) = 9.8*0.3700962 = 3.62694 m/s^2. Base: v^2 = 2*3.62694*4 = 29.0155, v = 5.3866 m/s. With the earlier 2 m on the same incline (TC409, TD27A) the block has slid 6 m from rest at the end of the stated distance: v^2 = 2*3.62694*6 = 43.5233, v = 6.5972 m/s. Mass (TDA34, T7D9C) cancels from a = g(sin - mu_k cos). Static friction 0.35 (T5DF8, T263F) only decides whether the block starts moving; tan 30 = 0.577 > 0.35 so it does. T0BDA: the bench slide precedes placement on the incline and release from rest, so it is disconnected. Variant groups state the same numbers and units: {T5DF8, T263F} 0.35; {TDA34, T7D9C} 2 kg; {TC409, TD27A, T0BDA} 2 m. Minor: TC409/TD27A re-anchor 'the stated distance' to begin 2 m after release, which the base problem implicitly places at the release point; the sentences make the re-anchoring explicit, so I do not count it as a contradiction. T7D9C adds 'solid wooden' which is harmless.
